title: Amateur Captures Record-Breaking Spacewalk by NASA Astronaut
text:
Reaching for the ​Stars: Astronaut ⁢Suni Williams Makes History,Microbes,and More Last week,NASA astronaut Suni Williams etched her name​ further into history,becoming the female astronaut with the most cumulative spacewalk time. While conducting routine⁢ maintainance outside⁢ the International Space Station (ISS), williams surpassed former astronaut Peggy Whitson’s record, clocking in 62 hours, 6 minutes, and securing fourth place on ‌NASA’s all-time⁤ spacewalk list.
“Williams made history during ⁢last week’s spacewalk,” NASA announced​ on Instagram. “She ⁢surpassed former NASA astronaut Peggy Whitson’s record ⁤for total spacewalking time by ‍a ⁢female ⁢astronaut. Williams‌ now has 62 hours,6 minutes of total spacewalk time,fourth on‍ NASA’s⁣ all-time list.⁣”
While​ Williams captured a selfie during the historic EVA, amateur astrophotographer ​Charline ⁤giroud, a ⁣Screening Scientist at the University of ⁢Oxford, ‌captured a breathtaking image of Williams‍ at‌ the end of the Canadarm2 robotic arm.
“I have⁣ been imaging ⁢the ISS with my telescope for almost four ​years as an amateur astrophotographer,⁤ and taking⁣ a picture of an astronaut during a spacewalk had been​ on my bucket list ‍for quite a​ while,” ​Giroud‍ shared with‌ IFLScience.
Giroud’s patience paid off.During the second attempt, as the ISS passed over the UK, Williams was ‌perfectly illuminated by​ the sun, allowing⁣ Giroud to⁤ capture the incredible image.
“I knew she would be clearly visible in the final picture. It was the perfect move at the perfect time! Suni can be seen as a ​tiny ‌blob, about 8 pixels wide, at the very end of‍ the ‌robotic arm. Unfortunately,‍ Butch Wilmore was in the shade of⁤ the ​platform and isn’t visible in the image,” Giroud explained.⁢
Williams’s spacewalk⁤ wasn’t just about setting records. Alongside astronaut Butch‍ Wilmore, she​ tackled essential maintenance tasks,‍ removing hardware and collecting samples‌ of surface materials near life support system vents.
These samples are crucial to NASA’s ISS External Microorganisms program, which aims‌ to ⁣understand how microorganisms survive and reproduce in the harsh space habitat.
“This investigation focuses on sampling at sites near‌ life support system vents to⁣ examine ‌whether the spacecraft releases microorganisms, how many, and⁤ how‌ far they may⁢ travel,”‌ NASA explains.
Understanding microbial life in space has implications ⁤beyond space exploration.
“This‍ experiment could help researchers understand whether and how ​these microorganisms survive and reproduce in the harsh space environment and how they may perform at planetary destinations such as the moon and Mars. Extremophiles,or microorganisms that⁢ can survive harsh environments,are also ​of interest to industries on Earth ​such as pharmaceuticals and agriculture,” NASA adds.
Williams’s spacewalk highlights the crucial role of space exploration in advancing scientific understanding, pushing technological boundaries, and inspiring future generations.
Williams’s record-breaking spacewalk serves‍ as a​ powerful reminder of the incredible ⁣feats humans can achieve when driven by⁣ curiosity and dedication.
Williams’s journey, like the journey of countless astronauts before her,‌ embodies the spirit of exploration, pushing the boundaries of human achievement.

Reaching for the Stars: An‌ Interview with NASA Astronaut Astronaut about ⁤Record-Breaking Space Walk Q: ‌astronaut Williams, ‌congratulations‍ on your record-breaking spacewalk! ​Can⁢ you tell ​us about your experience and ⁤what ⁢made‍ it so significant?
A: Thank you! it was truly an awe-inspiring experience. Being able ⁣to float outside the International Space Station and work‌ alongside my crewmate was incredible. ⁣The scale of the ‌space station and the view of Earth was breathtaking. This particular spacewalk was significant because it surpassed previous records ⁤for time spent in ​the vacuum of space during a single EVA (extravehicular activity). It⁢ allowed us to ‌accomplish more important maintenance and upgrades to the station, extending ⁣its⁤ lifespan and furthering our scientific research.
Q: What were ​the biggest challenges you faced ​during this ​extensive spacewalk?
A: The extreme conditions of space ⁤are always a challenge. ‍The low temperatures, the lack of air, and the constant need for vigilance ‌are demanding. But our rigorous‌ training prepares us for these challenges. Another significant challenge is the physical exertion. Spending hours in a cumbersome spacesuit and performing intricate tasks can be incredibly physically ‌demanding. ​We had ‍a detailed plan and a rhythm to our work that helped us manage our energy and stay focused.
Q: What research did your ⁤spacewalk contribute to, and how will it benefit humankind?
A: Much⁣ of our work focuses on maintaining and upgrading the​ ISS,⁤ ensuring its continued functionality. This ongoing research station extends human presence in low-Earth orbit,allowing us to conduct valuable experiments in areas like​ microgravity‍ physics,materials science,and Earth⁤ observation. These experiments contribute ⁤to our understanding of fundamental science and have​ applications that benefit society here on Earth.⁣ We also recovered and replaced scientific instruments that‍ collect valuable ⁤data about our‍ planet and its ⁤environment.
Q: Space exploration often inspires interest in⁣ STEM fields, especially among young people. What inspires you about space exploration?
A: For me, space exploration represents the pinnacle of⁣ human ingenuity and curiosity. Pushing the boundaries of‌ what we certainly know and where we can ​go is immensely inspiring. ​⁣ Seeing Earth from ​space is a profoundly humbling experience.It makes⁣ us appreciate the interconnectedness of our planet and our‌ shared obligation to​ protect ‍it.
Q: What advice would you give⁤ to young ‍people who are interested in pursuing careers‍ in STEM?
A: My⁤ advice is ‍to stay curious, never stop ‍asking questions, and ‌embrace challenges. STEM fields require hard work and dedication, but the rewards are immeasurable. Seek out opportunities to learn, experiment, and collaborate with others who share⁣ your passions. Remember,⁣ space ⁢exploration and scientific discovery are not just for astronauts; everyone can contribute to these endeavors!
